rationale: The workflow is a lint/test check triggered on push and pull_request to master, scoped to the charts/nfs-server-provisioner path. It currently has no concurrency control, so repeated pushes to the same branch or PR spawn duplicate runs that all execute to completion even when a newer revision supersedes an older one. The P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE pattern (cancel superseded runs) is supported by reviewed evidence (estimated VM-time reduction) and its scope is workflow_yaml. Its preconditions fit: runs represent the same workflow and branch/PR, and a newer revision supersedes older checks. Its contraindications do not apply: this is lint/test work, not release or deployment, and keying the concurrency group on github.ref keeps distinct branches and PRs in separate groups so they do not cancel each other. Adding a top-level concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true cancels stale in-progress runs when a newer revision starts while preserving the latest run's required-check coverage. No permissions are weakened, no secrets or privileged actions are added, no publishing/deployment or new network access is introduced, and all existing build/test steps are preserved unchanged.
